selected_experts.reason: Verify the fish's identity as a tench (Tinca tinca) by checking for key taxonomic features: small deeply embedded cycloid scales, olive-green to golden-bronze coloration, small head with blunt downturned mouth, two short barbels at each corner of the mouth, small eyes with reddish-orange iris, short rounded dorsal fin, truncate to slightly emarginate caudal fin, and a complete lateral line.
Locate specific anatomical features of the tench such as the barbels, fins (dorsal, caudal, pectoral, pelvic, anal), eyes, mouth, and lateral line to ensure they are present and correctly positioned.
Check for boundary integrity of the fish, ensuring fins are distinct and not fused with the body or background, and that the fish's outline is sharp and continuous without melting or fragmentation.

Assess the texture and appearance of the fish's skin to ensure it has the characteristic smooth, slimy, mucous-coated look of a tench, and check for any unnatural artifacts or distortions in the fish's body.

Verify the spatial relationship between the man and the fish, ensuring the fish is being held naturally in the man's hands with correct perspective and depth, and that the man's hands are properly interacting with the fish without distortion.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay special attention to the presence and position of the two short barbels at each corner of the mouth, the shape and ray count of the dorsal and caudal fins, the visibility of the lateral line, and the smooth, slimy texture of the skin. Ensure the fish's body proportions match the description (depth approximately 3-4 times standard length) and that the coloration transitions correctly from dorsal to ventral. Check that the man's hands are holding the fish naturally without any anatomical distortions.
